title: BLF: adding support for CAN-XL messages
description: Adding support for CAN-XL messages in BLF.

notes.body:
@giovanni.musto Can you test this?

@hartkopp please check.
I'm sorry, but unfortunately I don't have any log with CAN XL data.
Thnx. We found a way. :smile:

The SRR bit is the RTR substitution bit which is not relevant/visible for the user.
Did you think about the Remote Request Substitution (RRS) bit here?
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/3d497ddbdcbca5cd4e01ee32106cf62f6ebaf4df

Edit:
Oh, I've just seen that this fits the Vector BLF Spec like this.
Now I'm puzzled about SRR and RRS :smiley: 

https://www.can-cia.org/can-knowledge/can-fd-the-basic-idea

https://www.can-cia.org/can-knowledge/can-xl

I think we are talking about RRS in both cases.

The RRS bit can be used in some CAN XL controllers to extend the PRIO by one bit as it can be configured and accessed in the Controllers which has a direct effect on the arbitration.
Maybe Vector forgot the RRS for CAN-XL? Only in CAN-XL it seems that it does not have to be 0.

I think SRR and RRS all handle the RTR bit space. SRR is only relevant in 29 bit CAN IDs to postpone the RTR arbitration to the end (RTR in CAN CC, RRS in CAN FD/XL).

For CAN FD the RTR functionality has been abandoned (therefore RRS = 0).
And in CAN XL there's still no RTR functionality - but the bit is visible in the CAN controllers register - and writable in some of them too.
Therefore it can be used as an additional arbitration bit (default = 0).
This is a weird option and I hope no one will ever use it. Not sure whether all CAN XL controllers will ever support setting the RRS bit. I will add a controller config option for this in Linux.
So, what do we want to do?
Resolved.

This is not related to CAN XL changes.
You should split the editorial changes and beautifications into a separate patch.
